tagline: Return distinct values from a column and detect single slicer selections

slides.title: VALUES and SELECTEDVALUE
slides.body: VALUES(ColumnName) returns a one-column table of distinct, non-blank values from a column, respecting the current filter context. SELECTEDVALUE() is a shortcut that returns a scalar — the single selected value if exactly one is in context, otherwise an alternate result (default: BLANK()).
slides.keyPoint: VALUES = filtered table of distinct values. SELECTEDVALUE = scalar if exactly one value is in context, else alternate. Use them to detect slicer state and build dynamic calculations.

slides.title: FactSales — The Base Table
slides.caption: Used for all examples in this walkthrough

slides.title: VALUES() — No Filter Applied
slides.caption: All distinct Region values visible in the model
slides.expression:
-- VALUES returns a 1-column table:
VALUES(FactSales[Region])

-- Result (3 rows):
--   Region
--   -------
--   North
--   South
--   East
slides.explanation: With no slicer or report filter active, VALUES() returns all three distinct Region values from the table in the current filter context.

slides.title: User Selects 'North' in Region Slicer
slides.caption: Filter context now restricts visible rows to North only

slides.title: VALUES() — With 'North' Filter Active
slides.caption: Now only one distinct value is visible
slides.expression:
-- With 'North' slicer active:
VALUES(FactSales[Region])

-- Result (1 row):
--   Region
--   -------
--   North
slides.explanation: When the filter restricts the context to North rows only, VALUES() returns just 'North'. This is the basis for SELECTEDVALUE() — if VALUES() produces exactly one row, SELECTEDVALUE() returns that scalar.

slides.title: SELECTEDVALUE() — Dynamic Title or Label
slides.caption: Return the selected region name, or 'All Regions' if none/multiple
slides.expression:
SelectedRegionTitle =
    SELECTEDVALUE(
        FactSales[Region],
        "All Regions"  -- alternate result
    )

-- No slicer    → "All Regions"
-- North only   → "North"
-- North+South  → "All Regions"
slides.explanation: SELECTEDVALUE() checks: does VALUES(col) return exactly one row? If yes, return it as a scalar. If zero or more than one, return the alternate result. Use this for dynamic card titles, measure switches, or conditional logic.

slides.title: SELECTEDVALUE() in Conditional Calculations
slides.caption: Switch calculation logic based on a slicer selection
slides.expression:
-- Example: currency conversion controlled by slicer
Selected Currency =
    SELECTEDVALUE(DimCurrency[Code], "USD")

Revenue Converted =
    VAR currency = SELECTEDVALUE(DimCurrency[Code], "USD")
    VAR rate = LOOKUPVALUE(
        ExchangeRates[Rate],
        ExchangeRates[Code], currency
    )
    RETURN [Total Revenue] * rate
slides.explanation: A common PL-300 pattern: use SELECTEDVALUE() to detect what the user selected in a disconnected slicer table, then use that value to conditionally change the measure's behaviour.

slides.title: VALUES vs DISTINCT vs ALL — Know the Difference
bullets: VALUES(col) — distinct visible values in filter context, PLUS adds a blank row if a fact table references a key not in the dimension (referential integrity violation).
DISTINCT(col) — same as VALUES but NEVER includes the blank row from integrity violations. Use when you know your data is clean.
ALL(col) — ALL distinct values, IGNORING the current filter context. Used inside CALCULATE to remove filters: CALCULATE([Revenue], ALL(DimDate[Year])).
ALLEXCEPT(Table, col1, col2) — removes all filters from the table EXCEPT on the specified columns. Common in running total patterns.

Exam trap: VALUES() on a column with no referential integrity issues behaves identically to DISTINCT(). The difference only matters when an FK value in the fact table has no matching PK in the dimension.

slides.title: Common Exam Patterns
bullets: HASONEVALUE(col) is the boolean version: TRUE if exactly one value in context. Equivalent to COUNTROWS(VALUES(col)) = 1.
IF(HASONEVALUE(DimProduct[Category]), VALUES(DimProduct[Category]), "Multiple") is the same as SELECTEDVALUE(DimProduct[Category], "Multiple").
Pass VALUES() as a CALCULATE filter argument: CALCULATE([Sales], VALUES(DimDate[Year])) — this preserves the current year filter even inside a larger ALL context.
Use SELECTEDVALUE to build dynamic measure selectors (e.g., a slicer to choose between Revenue, Profit, or Margin as the displayed metric).
